Targeted estimation under a stochastic intensity intervention

Source: R/tmle-alpha.R
tmle_alpha.Rd

Estimates a target parameter under a stochastic intensity intervention that scales the intensity of the process z_name by alpha, optionally combined with an intervention a on the baseline treatment. The initial fit from fit_initial() is updated by iterative targeted maximum likelihood estimation (TMLE).

Usage

tmle_alpha(
  initial_fit,
  target,
  z_name = NULL,
  alpha = 1,
  alpha_list = NULL,
  a = NULL,
  estimand = c("risk", "years_lost"),
  only_first = FALSE,
  target_only_in_state = NULL,
  control = list(),
  cores = 1,
  verbose = FALSE
)

Arguments

initial_fit

An initial fit, as returned by fit_initial().

target

Character vector. Names of the target processes.

z_name

String. Name of the process in initial_fit whose intensity alpha scales. Required unless alpha = 1 or alpha_list is given.

alpha

Non-negative number. Multiplicative intervention on the intensity of z_name. alpha = 1 is no intervention.

alpha_list

Experimental, and may change. Optional named list of functions, one per process, giving a time-varying multiplicative intervention on that process's intensity. Each function is called with the columns of initial_fit$tmp_long named by its arguments, e.g. time, a baseline covariate such as L0, or a process such as z (its number of jumps so far), and must return one non-negative factor per row. For example, list(z = function(time) ifelse(time < 0.5, 0.5, 1)) halves the intensity of z before time 0.5. Cannot be combined with alpha and z_name.

a

Optional baseline treatment value (0 or 1) to intervene on. Must be one of the arms prepared by fit_initial().

estimand

The target parameter: "risk", the risk of target by tau (or the expected number of events for a recurrent target), or "years_lost", the expected time lost, i.e. the integral of the risk of target up to tau.

only_first

Logical. If TRUE, only the first target event counts, and only the first jump of z_name is intervened on.

target_only_in_state

Experimental, and may change. Optional function of the state space initial_fit$depend_matrix, a data frame with one row per state and a column per process that other processes depend on (its number of jumps), returning a logical vector marking the states in which target events count. For example, function(states) states[["z"]] == 0 counts only deaths before illness.

control

A named list of settings for how the estimate is computed:

  • one_step (FALSE): if TRUE, return the one-step estimator instead of iterating the TMLE update.

  • block_size (10): positive integer. For estimand = "years_lost", the integral is approximated by evaluating the risk once per block of block_size consecutive time points. 1 gives the exact integral of the estimated risk; the computation time is roughly proportional to 1 / block_size.

  • target_by_state (FALSE): if TRUE, use state-specific clever covariates in the targeting step.

  • conv_const (1): positive number. The TMLE iterations stop when the absolute mean of the efficient influence curve falls below conv_const * se / log(n).

  • max_iter (10): maximum number of TMLE iterations.

  • min_iter (0): minimum number of TMLE iterations before checking convergence.

  • truncate_weights (Inf): positive number at which the clever weights of the intervention are truncated. Inf is no truncation.

cores

Positive integer. Number of cores used by parallel::mclapply() for the per-individual computations.

verbose

Logical. If TRUE, print progress.

Value

An object of class tmle_alpha, a list with elements:

  • estimate: a data.table with one row per target and columns target, estimate, its standard error se, and the bounds lower and upper of a 95% Wald confidence interval.

  • initial_estimate: the initial plug-in estimates, before targeting, named by target.

  • method: "tmle", or "one_step" if control$one_step = TRUE.

  • estimand: as given.

  • alpha, z_name and a: the intervention (alpha is NULL if alpha_list is given).

  • eic: a list, named by target, with the efficient influence curve, one value per individual.

  • checks: a list of diagnostics:

    • iter, eic_solved_at and converged: vectors, named by target, of the number of iterations, the absolute mean of the efficient influence curve, and whether the iterations converged. A warning is given if they did not.

    • weights: a matrix with the quantiles (columns q50, q90, q99 and q100) over individuals of each individual's maximal intervention, censoring and treatment weight, and of their product total, the weight entering the targeting step (rows), as a positivity diagnostic. The intervention weights are those after truncation, and the treatment weights are 1 when a is not given.

    • n_truncated: the number of individuals whose initial intervention weight was truncated (0 if control$truncate_weights = Inf).

    weights and n_truncated are shared by the targets; with only_first and several targets, they are those of the first.

Details

By default the target parameter is the risk of a target event by the horizon tau given to fit_initial() (or the expected number of events for a recurrent target). Several targets are estimated separately, under the same intervention.

The functions in alpha_list and target_only_in_state are called as described in the section "Functions in the arguments" of fit_initial().

Examples

fit <- fit_initial(
  illness_death,
  fit_types = list(
    z = list(
      delta = 2,
      model = ~ L0,
      at_risk = function(dt) dt[["z"]] == 0
    ),
    death = list(delta = 1, model = ~ L0 + z),
    censoring = list(delta = 0, model = ~ L0)
  ),
  tau = 1
)

# Risk of death by tau = 1 if the intensity of z were halved.
est <- tmle_alpha(fit, target = "death", z_name = "z", alpha = 0.5)
est$estimate
#>    target  estimate         se     lower     upper
#>    <char>     <num>      <num>     <num>     <num>
#> 1:  death 0.3040549 0.03853505 0.2285276 0.3795823
